beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Three weeks into her first real studio sessions, Riley's still getting used to someone else calling the shots in the room.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "The producer keeps telling me to trust the process, even when I have no idea what he's doing to the vocal take. Strange, taking direction again after a year of just doing it myself."

options.text: Trusting the process doesn't mean trusting it blindly — it means trusting him specifically.
You should never let anyone else touch your vocals.
Trusting a process and trusting a person are unrelated.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I guess I do trust him. I just don't love not understanding what's happening."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: This is exactly that — a message that arrives through someone you actually trust, not through figuring it out alone.
It means you should never take a note from anyone again.
This card has nothing to do with taking direction.

elaboration: The message here doesn't have to arrive on its own — it comes through a mentor, a teacher, or a structure you've decided to trust.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Doesn't that make me the least DIY person in the room, letting someone else steer?"

options.text: Not at all — spiritual truth here doesn't ask you to give up your own instincts to use it.
Yes, DIY and taking direction can't coexist.
This card has no opinion on independence.

elaboration: Spiritual truth doesn't have to abandon the pleasures of daily life — leaning on a trusted structure and keeping your own voice were never actually opposites.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Yeah. I think I can let him drive for a few takes and still know it's mine."
